title: Neuromodulation of Sleep and Mood: A Multimodal Biomarker Study of Non-Invasive Vagal Nerve Stimulation (MOSAIC-VNS)
official: Neuromodulation of Sleep and Mood: A Multimodal Biomarker Study of Non-Invasive Vagal Nerve Stimulation (MOSAIC-VNS)
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* To be eligible, participants must meet all of the following criteria:

  1. Adults aged 18 through 50 years, inclusive, at the time of consent.
  2. Able to understand and provide written informed consent in English.
  3. Willing and able to wear a study-provided wrist-worn device continuously for approximately 6 weeks and to complete daily sleep diaries.
  4. Willing and able to self-administer the study device twice daily for 6 weeks and to complete a device use log.
  5. Access to a smartphone compatible with the study wearable platform, or willingness to use a study-provided device.
  6. Regular sleep opportunity of at least 6 hours per 24-hour period.

     Cohort A (symptomatic) - additional inclusion criteria:
  7. Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) total score ≥ 15 at screening and confirmed at Visit 1.
  8. MADRS total score ≥ 20 at screening and confirmed at Visit 1.
  9. Meets DSM-5-TR criteria for insomnia disorder on structured clinical interview.
  10. If receiving psychotropic medication or psychotherapy, the regimen has been stable for at least 6 weeks before Visit 1, and the participant and treating clinician agree it will remain stable through Visit 3.

      Cohort B (healthy reference) - additional inclusion criteria:
  11. ISI total score ≤ 7 and MADRS total score ≤ 8 at screening and confirmed at Visit 1.
  12. No current psychiatric disorder or sleep disorder as established by structured diagnostic interview.
  13. No psychotropic medication use within the prior 30 days.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Participants meeting any of the following criteria are not eligible:

  1. Night-shift or rotating-shift work within the 30 days before Visit 1, or planned during participation.
  2. Travel across more than two time zones within the 14 days before Visit 1, or planned during participation.
  3. Any contraindication to cervical nVNS, including an implanted cervical electrical or metallic device, cardiac pacemaker or implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, any other implanted electronic device, clinically significant carotid atherosclerosis, prior cervical vagotomy, carotid endarterectomy, or cervical surgery at the application site.
  4. Open wound, skin breakdown, active infection, or a dermatologic condition at the intended application site.
  5. Known or suspected pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Participants of childbearing potential will undergo urine pregnancy testing at screening..
  6. Clinically significant cardiac arrhythmia, uncontrolled hypertension (systolic ≥ 160 or diastolic ≥ 100 mmHg on repeated measurement), congestive heart failure, or syncope of unclear cause.
  7. Untreated moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea (STOP-Bang ≥ 5 without evaluation and clearance), restless legs syndrome requiring pharmacologic treatment, narcolepsy, or a circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder.
  8. Moderate or severe substance or alcohol use disorder within the prior 6 months, or a positive urine drug screen for a non-prescribed substance judged to affect sleep or autonomic measures.
  9. Lifetime diagnosis of bipolar I disorder, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, or another primary psychotic disorder.
  10. Active suicidal ideation with intent or plan (C-SSRS ideation type 4 or 5), any suicide attempt within the prior 6 months, or any clinical presentation requiring urgent or higher-level psychiatric care.
  11. Use of an alternative neuromodulation therapy (implanted VNS, transcranial magnetic stimulation, transcranial direct current stimulation, or electroconvulsive therapy) within the prior 3 months.
  12. Initiation of, or change in dose of, any medication with known substantial effects on heart rate variability (for example, beta-blockers, anticholinergics) within 6 weeks before Visit 1.
  13. Any medical, neurological, or psychiatric condition that, in the investigator's judgment, would compromise participant safety, adherence, or interpretation of study measures.
